message.content:
**July 4, 1776** – That’s when the Second Continental Congress formally **adopted** the text of the Declaration of Independence.  

While the document itself was approved on that day, the actual act of signing didn’t happen all at once. Most delegates began affixing their signatures shortly thereafter—many did so during sessions from August through October 1776—but additional copies were printed and more signatures were added up until early 1778. So while “signed” often refers to those subsequent dates, the official adoption—and what people usually mean by “the Declaration was signed”—was on July 4, 1776.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: When was the Declaration of Independence signed? They want a factual answer: July 4, 1776 (though signing occurred over time). But historically, the Continental Congress adopted it on July 4, 1776; signatures were added later, with most signers adding their names between August and December 1777.

Thus we can respond concisely: It was adopted on July 4, 1776, but formal signing took place mostly after that, culminating around late 1777. Provide context. No tool needed.
